page.layout: One page of running text, one column, with text in the left margin area and short lines in the body. No margin notes. Running head at top; page number at top left.

main_text.p: Sic Lectus. Auditus, Latus sim vel fuerim, sis vel fueris, sit vel fuerit, &c.
main_text.head: Primum plusquam perfectum tempus.
main_text.p: Amatus eram vel fueram, ich was geliebet / eras, vel fueras, erat vel fuerat, amati eramus vel fueramus, eratis, vel fueratis, erant vel fuerant.
Doctus eram vel fueram, ich was gelehret / eras vel fueras, erat vel fuerat, docti eramus vel fueramus, eratis vel fueratis, erant vel fuerant.
Sic Lectus, Auditus, Latus eram vel fueram, eras vel fueras, erat vel fuerat, &c.
main_text.head: Secundum plusquam perfectum tempus.
main_text.p: Amatus essem vel fuissem, ich were geliebet worden / esses vel fuisses, esset vel fuisset, amati essemus vel fuissemus, essetis vel fuissetis, essent vel fuissent.
Doctus essem vel fuissem, ich were gelehret worden/esses vel fuisses, esset vel fuisset, docti essemus vel fuissemus, essetis vel fuissetis, essent vel fuissent.
Sic Lectus, Auditus, Latus essem vel fuissem, esses vel fuisses, esset vel fuisset, &c.
Scimus quidem perfectorum temporum periphrasin ad Syntaxin pertinere: tamen ne studiosi de Ramea Grammatices difficultate quererentur, voluimus circunloquendi formam subjicere.
main_text.head: Primum futurum tempus.
main_text.p: Amabor, ich wil oder werde oder sol geliebet werden / amaberis vel amabere, amabitur, amabimur, amabimini, amabuntur.
Docebor, doceberis vel docebere, docebitur, docebimur, docebimini, docebuntur.
Legar, legeris vel legere, legetur, legemur, legemini, legentur.
Audiar, audieris vel audiere, audietur, audiemur, audiemini, audientur.

page.notes: Printed German words in black letter within the Latin text are rendered in plain type here; the page shows heavy mixed black letter and roman for German glosses. The word "Ramea" (Ramea Grammatices) appears as printed, likely Ramea (Ramus). Line "Ferar," at the foot is a catchword-like fragment and is kept as the last line of text. Some lines are faint at the edges; the reading of "Doctus eram" German gloss "gelehret" is taken from the scan with [?] where uncertain. Paragraph breaks in the verb paradigm lines are set by the printer's indents as best read.
